newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil bolsas create 2nd over-the-counter bourse.
newsitem.headline: Brazil bolsas create 2nd over-the-counter bourse.

text.p: South America's largest bourse, seven other Brazilian bolsas and six companies have joined forces to create Brazil's second Nasdaq-like over-the-counter stock market, officials said.

The new Mercado Brasileiro de Balcao (MBB), which would operate from the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa), would compete for business with Rio de Janeiro's two-month-old SOMA over-the-counter bourse, they said.

MBB President Afonso Arno Arnhold told reporters the new bolsa would initially cater to small and medium-sized firms with sales of up to 100 million reais and could begin operating in a month following approval from Brazil's Securities Commission (CVM).

Officials of the Sao Paulo bourse, the BM&F futures exchange, six regional bolsas and six firms formally agreed Friday to create the bolsa, with authorized capital of 5.0 million reais and 722,000 reais in start-up funds, he said.

The market would directly compete with the SOMA, an over-the-counter market created by the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange and other partners. But MBB officials insist the intention was not to undermine the Rio OTC bourse.
"The two projects were born simultaneously," said Alfredo Rizkallah, head of the Sao Paulo exchange and MBB general manager. "There was no agreement between us but there was no disagreement either."

He said the MBB is not looking to compete with the SMA but rather looking for Brazilian capital markets to grow, adding that competition between the bolsas would be positive as it would keep costs down for investors and brokers.
Currently, 916 Brazilian firms are publically registered with the CVM, of which 550 have shares trading on local bourses.
"That leaves a substantial potential market for the MBB," Arnhold said.

Rizkallah said the MBB would use Bovespa's infrastructure, including an electronic trading method, and would charge a $2,500 a year registration fee for small and medium-sized firms and as well as a 0.035 percent rate per transaction.

The SOMA, known as the Sociedade Operadora de Mercado de Aceso, was founded in November and in two months has shown stronger-than-expected growth, trading daily some 6.5 million reais, officials said.

Rizkallah and Arnhold said they did not have volume or projections or targets for the MBB but said it has could initially list some 30 to 50 firms and has a promising future due to the changes underway in the Brazilian economy.
"With privatization, Brazil is drawing a significant amount of foreign investment. Internal savings are also on the rise," Arnhold said.
